text: The gap appears because the present state satisfies only the physical needs.  Without the other two essential elements—healthy relationships with others and the right self‑understanding—human aspirations for continuous happiness and prosperity cannot be fully realized.  When an individual lives for physical facility alone, the consciousness remains animal‑like; only by adding relational and cognitive dimensions does one achieve the holistic development that transforms the gap into a fulfilled state.

We are working on holistic development—transforming from animal to human consciousness. This involves ensuring physical facility, building relationships with other human beings, and cultivating the right understanding within the self. Education–sanskar plays a key role in enabling this transformation and thereby filling the aspiration for continuous happiness and prosperity.
It is getting filled. Through holistic development, the gap between mere physical needs and the full human aspiration for happiness and prosperity is progressively filled, rather than widening.

Based on the lesson, physical facility alone is necessary but not adequate for human happiness. The other two factors—healthy relationships with people and right understanding of the self—are also required. Therefore, if the family feels unhappy, the cause is more likely to be a lack of fulfilment in relationships than a lack of physical resources.

Physical comfort is essential but it alone cannot provide lasting satisfaction. To achieve true fulfilment, you must allocate comparable or even greater time and effort to nurturing relationships and cultivating self‑understanding, giving these areas as much priority as the material basics.

text: For animals, physical facility (with nature) is sufficient for their needs. For humans, physical facility is necessary but insufficient - we also require meaningful relationships (interpersonal connections) and right understanding (self-awareness and philosophical wisdom). This makes humans capable of seeking higher consciousness (human consciousness with balanced priorities) compared to animals which live solely for physical gratification (animal consciousness).

text: Holistic development refers to the transformation from animal consciousness (focusing only on physical facility) to human consciousness (balancing physical facility, relationships with others, and right understanding within the self). The role of education–sanskar is to facilitate this transformative process by prioritizing these three elements, enabling individuals to transcend mere physical needs and cultivate a harmonious existence with nature, society, and self-awareness.

This hierarchy distinguishes human existence from purely materialistic animal-like living.
